sharedDesign.professorPattern: diagnose briefly, teach one idea, learner attempt, graded hint, retry, transfer
sharedDesign.evaluationBoundary: Only demonstrated learner responses count. Reference answers, help requests and local exercise completion are not learner evidence.
sharedDesign.publicationGate: Source review + authored-content QA + local tests + separate database publication decision.

finance_revenue.workingTitle: Revenue judgement: contracts, performance obligations & cut-off
finance_revenue.goal: Apply the IFRS 15 five-step model to a compact close scenario and explain what evidence is still needed before booking or deferring revenue.

sections.title: Start with the contract and promised transfer
sections.focus: Identify the customer contract and distinct promised goods/services before jumping to an invoice or GL account.

sections.title: Transaction price and timing are separate judgements
sections.focus: Separate what consideration is expected from when control of each promise transfers.

sections.title: Close evidence: invoice date is not the whole answer
sections.focus: Use delivery/service evidence, contractual terms and cut-off controls; distinguish billing from revenue recognition.

sections.title: Irish statutory bridge without framework mixing
sections.focus: If the local entity applies FRS 102, scope the applicable 2026 revenue requirements separately rather than copying the group IFRS conclusion automatically.

finance_revenue.case: Fictional year-end contract contains hardware delivered on 29 December, a separately identifiable support service beginning 1 January, and an invoice for both dated 28 December. Learner must identify what facts determine recognition and design one cut-off control; amounts are supplied only after the recognition logic is established.
assessmentMustDistinguish: IFRS group package versus local FRS 102 basis

officialSources.supports: Current FRS 102 edition and Periodic Review 2024 effective-date context for UK/Republic of Ireland

payroll_submission.workingTitle: RPN, pay date, Employment ID & payroll submission workflow
payroll_submission.goal: Run the evidence sequence from employee/employment identity and RPN through pay date and submission, then diagnose a fictional exception without inventing tax treatment.

sections.title: Identify the employment before calculating
sections.focus: Separate employee identity from the Employment ID used for each employment/period of employment.

sections.title: Use the correct RPN for the pay period
sections.focus: Retrieve/use the applicable RPN; do not reuse the prior year's notification or invent credits when unavailable.

sections.title: Pay date controls the reporting period
sections.focus: Connect actual payment timing to the payroll submission and retain the payroll-run reference/audit trail.

sections.title: Submission exception: diagnose before correcting
sections.focus: Distinguish wrong input, wrong identifier, missing RPN and wrong pay date; use the correction path supported by Revenue rather than forcing net pay to prior month.

payroll_submission.case: Fictional employee has unchanged salary but the first 2026 run references an old RPN and a payroll file contains a changed Employment ID. Learner must identify which facts are definitely wrong, what should be retrieved/reconciled and what cannot yet be concluded about the tax amount.
assessmentMustDistinguish: employee-facing explanation versus internal audit trail
current Revenue rule versus fictional amount

officialSources.supports: 2026 RPN availability/use and emergency basis when unavailable

english_meetings.goal: Participate naturally in a work meeting: clarify an ambiguous point, check understanding, state a view concisely and reconnect after a short detour.

sections.title: Enter the conversation without over-formality
sections.focus: Signal a relevant contribution and connect it to the previous speaker rather than delivering a memorised mini-speech.

sections.title: Clarify before disagreeing
sections.focus: Use concise clarification/paraphrase language to confirm what the other person means before challenging it.

sections.title: State a view with evidence and uncertainty
sections.focus: Give headline, reason and caveat; avoid hiding behind excessive softening or claiming certainty that the facts do not support.

sections.title: Repair and follow up
sections.focus: Handle misunderstanding, interruption or a side question, then reconnect to the meeting objective with one useful follow-up.

english_meetings.case: Fictional cross-functional meeting about a monthly variance. The explanation is ambiguous about whether the issue is timing or a real cost increase. Learner must ask one clarifying question, summarise the answer, give a concise view and propose the next check.

officialSources.supports: Business English workplace communication and interview/email resources
Advanced meetings, talks and job-interview listening contexts
B2 workplace talks, presentations, dialogues and relationship/conflict themes
